variants.title: Run the layout path
variants.context: A layout-aware path keeps four contracts separate: render and normalize the page at a recorded scale, detect candidate regions with a pinned model, recognize and relate content, then validate coverage and provenance before publishing a versioned result.
variants.prompt: A scanned journal page arrives and the product needs typed regions from it. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Detect candidate boxes, classes, and confidence scores with a pinned model and backend.
Validate coverage, sequence, provenance, and downstream requirements before publishing a versioned result.
Run OCR only where it is needed, then resolve columns, captions, tables, and reading order.
Render and normalize the page at a bounded size and record the transform between source coordinates and pixels.

variants.hint: Which stage has to exist before a box coordinate means anything?
variants.explanation: The render transform is recorded first because every later box, crop, and review action is expressed against that coordinate system.

variants.title: Run the layout path
variants.context: A layout-aware path keeps four contracts separate: render and normalize the page at a recorded scale, detect candidate regions with a pinned model, recognize and relate content, then validate coverage and provenance before publishing a versioned result.
variants.prompt: A figure and its caption must survive into the published output as related regions. Put the work in order.

items.text: Apply the confidence floor and class-aware suppression so the caption is not deleted as a figure duplicate.
Recognize the caption text inside its own region rather than across the whole page.
Attach the caption to the figure by containment and adjacency in the ordering stage.
Validate that both regions appear in the published sequence exactly once.
Detect the figure box and the caption box as separate typed regions with their own scores.

variants.hint: A box detector never returns the relationship; something later has to build it.
variants.explanation: Detection produces regions and structure is constructed afterwards, so the caption link is an ordering decision that must be stored and checked.

variants.title: Run the layout path
variants.context: A layout-aware path keeps four contracts separate: render and normalize the page at a recorded scale, detect candidate regions with a pinned model, recognize and relate content, then validate coverage and provenance before publishing a versioned result.
variants.prompt: A new parser environment is a candidate for the default. Put the release path in order.

items.text: Preserve the previous model, policy, and output schema as a rollback target.
Compare region, order, downstream, latency, and memory gates by slice.
Store the exact source and transforms needed to reproduce any disputed result.
Replay the golden corpus with the candidate environment on stored inputs.
Shadow or canary the candidate without overwriting accepted results.

variants.hint: Nothing live is touched until one thing has been rerun.
variants.explanation: Replaying stored inputs first isolates the environment change, and canarying without overwriting accepted results is what keeps the release reversible.

variants.title: Reconstruct the reading order
variants.context: Reading order is constructed, not observed. A useful ordering stage places spanning regions such as titles and footers, resolves lane membership before local vertical order, attaches captions and notes by containment and adjacency, and falls back to explicit predecessor links when geometry stays ambiguous.
variants.prompt: A two-column article page carries a page title, a sidebar, and a repeated footer. Put the ordering decisions in order.

items.text: Attach captions, notes, and the sidebar by containment and adjacency to what they belong to.
Check that every source region appears in the final sequence exactly once.
Place spanning regions such as the page title before any column content.
Assign every remaining region to a column or lane.
Order regions vertically inside each lane rather than across the whole page.

variants.hint: Lane membership has to be settled before vertical position means anything.
variants.explanation: Sorting by vertical position alone interleaves columns, so lanes are resolved first and the coverage check proves nothing was lost or duplicated.

variants.title: Reconstruct the reading order
variants.context: Reading order is constructed, not observed. A useful ordering stage places spanning regions such as titles and footers, resolves lane membership before local vertical order, attaches captions and notes by containment and adjacency, and falls back to explicit predecessor links when geometry stays ambiguous.
variants.prompt: A table splits across a page break and its continuation carries no repeated header. Put the handling in order.

items.text: Record an explicit predecessor relationship linking the continuation to the first fragment.
Detect the table regions on both pages as separate typed regions.
Resolve each page's lanes so neither table fragment is interleaved with body text.
Publish the sequence with that relationship stored alongside the regions.

variants.hint: Geometry alone cannot express a link that crosses a page break.
variants.explanation: Explicit predecessor relationships are the fallback when geometry is ambiguous, and storing them makes the chosen sequence reviewable later.

variants.title: Reconstruct the reading order
variants.context: Reading order is constructed, not observed. A useful ordering stage places spanning regions such as titles and footers, resolves lane membership before local vertical order, attaches captions and notes by containment and adjacency, and falls back to explicit predecessor links when geometry stays ambiguous.
variants.prompt: Reviewers report that a repeated footer keeps appearing in the middle of the article text. Put the diagnosis in order.

items.text: Check whether the ordering stage treated it as a spanning region or as body content.
Reproduce the sequence from the stored ordering decision and policy version.
Confirm the footer was detected as its own typed region with its own class.
Change the ordering policy so spanning regions are placed outside lane order.
Replay the golden corpus to confirm no other document family regressed.

variants.hint: The published sequence was a recorded decision, so it can be replayed rather than guessed at.
variants.explanation: Storing the chosen sequence and its policy version is what turns an ordering complaint into a reproducible defect instead of an argument.

variants.title: Count what the region policy keeps
variants.context: A confidence floor and non-maximum suppression are policies, not measures of truth. Raising the floor removes false positives and real captions alike, and class-aware suppression compares same-class overlap so a caption inside a figure is not deleted as a duplicate.
variants.prompt: A page produces 14 raw detections. The 0.55 confidence floor removes 5 of them, and class-aware suppression then removes 3 same-class duplicates. How many regions are published?
variants.hint: Suppression only sees what the floor left behind.
variants.explanation: The floor and the suppression step are two separate policies applied in order, so the published count is the raw detections minus both.

mistakes.feedback: Only the confidence floor was applied; the duplicate boxes still had to be suppressed.
Only the suppression step was applied; the low-confidence detections were never dropped.

variants.title: Count what the region policy keeps
variants.context: A confidence floor and non-maximum suppression are policies, not measures of truth. Raising the floor removes false positives and real captions alike, and class-aware suppression compares same-class overlap so a caption inside a figure is not deleted as a duplicate.
variants.prompt: A page has 20 detections: 12 score at or above 0.80, 5 score between 0.55 and 0.79, and 3 score below 0.55. The floor is raised from 0.55 to 0.80. How many additional regions does the raise drop?
variants.hint: The three weakest boxes were already gone before the raise.
variants.explanation: Raising a floor only removes detections that used to pass it, which is exactly how a valid caption sitting in the middle band disappears.

mistakes.feedback: The 3 detections already below the old floor were counted again as new losses.
That is the number of regions that survive the higher floor, not the number newly dropped.

variants.title: Count what the region policy keeps
variants.context: A confidence floor and non-maximum suppression are policies, not measures of truth. Raising the floor removes false positives and real captions alike, and class-aware suppression compares same-class overlap so a caption inside a figure is not deleted as a duplicate.
variants.prompt: A page yields 18 detections across three classes. Class-aware suppression removes 4 same-class duplicates. A misconfigured run used class-agnostic suppression instead and removed 7 boxes. How many valid regions did the misconfigured run delete?
variants.hint: Compare what each policy removed, not what each policy left.
variants.explanation: Class-agnostic suppression deletes overlapping boxes of different classes, which is how a caption sitting inside a figure gets removed as a duplicate.

mistakes.feedback: That is how many regions survive the misconfigured run, not how many valid ones it deleted.
That is the survivor count under correct class-aware suppression.

variants.title: Attach evidence to its stage
variants.context: Every emitted region stays traceable to its source page, coordinates, class, confidence, model and configuration version, and later ordering decision. Each stage records its own evidence, and OCR evidence is stored separately from detector evidence.
variants.prompt: A region record is being designed. Match each stage to the evidence it must record.

pairs.label: Render and normalize
pairs.detail: Original page size, rendered image size, rotation, crop, and scale.

pairs.label: Detect regions
pairs.detail: Model URI, label map, backend, score floor, box, class, and confidence.

pairs.label: Recognize text
pairs.detail: OCR engine, language, image transform, word boxes, and recognition confidence.

pairs.label: Relate and publish
pairs.detail: The chosen region sequence, predecessor relationships, and the coverage check.

variants.hint: Two stages describe pixels and two describe meaning.
variants.explanation: Recording each stage's evidence separately is what lets a failure be attributed, because a bad crop and a bad recognition look identical in the final text.

variants.title: Attach evidence to its stage
variants.context: Every emitted region stays traceable to its source page, coordinates, class, confidence, model and configuration version, and later ordering decision. Each stage records its own evidence, and OCR evidence is stored separately from detector evidence.
variants.prompt: Four defects are reported on one published page. Match each defect to the stage evidence you would read first.

pairs.label: A valid caption never appears in the output at all
The published text interleaves the left and right columns
A crop lands partly outside the page boundary
The box is correct but the characters inside it are garbled

variants.hint: Ask which stage was the last one that could still have been right.
variants.explanation: Attribution follows the evidence chain, so a garbled string points at recognition while a lost region points at the detection policy.

variants.title: Attach evidence to its stage
variants.context: Every emitted region stays traceable to its source page, coordinates, class, confidence, model and configuration version, and later ordering decision. Each stage records its own evidence, and OCR evidence is stored separately from detector evidence.
variants.prompt: A second page raises four more defects. Match each to the stage evidence that explains it.

pairs.label: Two boxes cover the same paragraph and its text is published twice
A figure caption is published far away from the figure it describes
Every box on the page is offset by a constant amount after a rotation
A Greek passage came back as unrelated Latin characters

variants.hint: A constant offset across every box points at something shared by all of them.
variants.explanation: A systematic offset is a transform problem rather than a detector problem, which is why the coordinate transform is stored instead of being recomputed later.

variants.title: Pin what a result depends on
variants.context: A model URI, label map, backend, framework build, and score floor form one tested deployment artifact, and a threshold validated on one document family is not evidence about another. Provenance travels with the result so a disputed page can be reproduced.
variants.prompt: To avoid redeploys, a team proposes having the request handler download the newest detector weights on first use. What should the reviewer say?
options: Approve it if the handler caches the download and retries on network failure.
Approve it, since the model URI names a specific version each time it runs.
Reject it, and load digest-verified artifacts at worker start from a pinned build.
optionFeedback: Caching hides the problem rather than removing it, and inference should not need network access at all.
Naming a version at request time still lets two workers serve the same page under different models.
Model URI, label map, backend, build, and score floor form one tested artifact that is pinned and verified at start.
variants.hint: Ask what two workers would have to share for their results to be comparable.
variants.explanation: The complete environment is one deployment artifact, so it is pinned, built in CI, and replayed against a golden corpus before it becomes the default.

variants.title: Pin what a result depends on
variants.context: A model URI, label map, backend, framework build, and score floor form one tested deployment artifact, and a threshold validated on one document family is not evidence about another. Provenance travels with the result so a disputed page can be reproduced.
variants.prompt: An overlap threshold tuned on native journal renders is about to be reused for scanned invoices on a new template. What is the right move?
options: Lower it across all families so the new template cannot lose any regions.
Reuse it unchanged, because overlap is geometry and geometry is document independent.
Re-evaluate it on the new family, scan conditions, and region classes before adopting.
optionFeedback: A global change trades a possible loss on one family for duplicate regions everywhere else.
The threshold encodes how that model's boxes behaved on one family, not a universal property of geometry.
A threshold is evidence about the corpus it was measured on and has to be measured again on new templates and conditions.
variants.hint: Ask what corpus the current number is actually evidence about.
variants.explanation: Thresholds are policies validated per document family, language, scan condition, and region class rather than constants carried between corpora.

variants.title: Pin what a result depends on
variants.context: A model URI, label map, backend, framework build, and score floor form one tested deployment artifact, and a threshold validated on one document family is not evidence about another. Provenance travels with the result so a disputed page can be reproduced.
variants.prompt: A customer disputes the reading order on a page parsed six weeks ago, and the pipeline has changed twice since. What makes the dispute answerable?
options: Replay the stored source and transforms under the recorded parser and policy versions.
Keep the rendered page image so a reviewer can judge the order by eye.
Rerun the page through the current pipeline and compare it with the complaint.
optionFeedback: Stored source, transforms, and version identity are what reproduce the original decision rather than a new one.
An image shows what the page looked like but not which ordering policy produced the published sequence.
The current pipeline produces a different result and says nothing about what the customer was actually served.
variants.hint: Ask what would have to be recreated to see the original decision again.
variants.explanation: Storing the source, transforms, and version identity of every result is what makes a past decision reproducible after the pipeline moves on.
